CommonQuestions.Title: Frequently asked questions about taxation in Switzerland

Questions.Question: When should I register for VAT in Geneva and what are the requirements?
Questions.Answer: Companies must register for VAT in Switzerland when annual turnover exceeds CHF 100,000. Registration involves submitting forms to the Federal Tax Administration, providing business documentation, and setting up quarterly or semi-annual VAT reporting. We guide you through the entire process, ensuring compliance with Geneva cantonal requirements and helping you understand input tax deductions, VAT rates, and electronic filing obligations through the SwissDeclaration portal.

Questions.Question: What are the tax filing deadlines for individuals and companies in Switzerland?
Questions.Answer: Individual tax returns in Geneva are typically due by March 31st following the tax year, with possible extensions until September or November. Corporate tax returns depend on your fiscal year-end and are usually due within six months. Missing deadlines can result in penalties and estimated assessments. We maintain a comprehensive calendar for all your tax obligations, including advance payments, withholding tax submissions, and VAT declarations, ensuring you never miss a critical deadline.

Questions.Question: How can I optimize my tax situation as a small or medium enterprise in Switzerland?
Questions.Answer: Tax optimization for SMEs involves strategic planning across multiple areas: choosing the optimal legal structure (Sàrl vs SA), maximizing deductible business expenses, timing of investments and depreciation, pension contributions for directors and employees, and leveraging cantonal tax incentives. Geneva and Vaud offer specific advantages for certain industries. We analyze your complete situation, including personal and corporate taxation, to develop tailored strategies that legally minimize your tax burden while maintaining full compliance with Swiss federal and cantonal regulations.

Questions.Question: How do dual taxation agreements affect international businesses operating in Switzerland?
Questions.Answer: Switzerland has signed over 100 double taxation agreements protecting businesses from being taxed twice on the same income. These agreements determine which country has primary taxing rights based on factors like residency, permanent establishment, and income source. For international clients operating in Geneva, we analyze treaty provisions, determine your tax residency status, handle treaty relief applications, and coordinate with foreign tax advisors. This ensures optimal tax positioning while managing cross-border compliance obligations in all relevant jurisdictions.

Questions.Question: What should I expect during a tax audit in Geneva or Vaud canton?
Questions.Answer: Tax audits in Swiss cantons are professional processes where authorities verify the accuracy of your declarations. They typically request detailed documentation including accounting records, contracts, invoices, and correspondence. Audits can be random or triggered by discrepancies. We prepare comprehensive documentation packages, represent you in all communications with tax authorities, explain technical accounting treatments, and negotiate settlements when necessary. Our experience with Geneva and Lausanne tax administrations helps ensure audits proceed smoothly with minimal business disruption and optimal outcomes.

Questions.Question: What are withholding tax obligations for companies employing foreign workers in Switzerland?
Questions.Answer: Employers must withhold tax at source for foreign employees without a C permit or Swiss/EU citizens without a settlement permit. Rates vary by canton, income level, and family situation. In Geneva, monthly withholding tax declarations are mandatory, with annual reconciliations required. We calculate correct withholding amounts, prepare monthly submissions, handle rate adjustments for changing situations, manage annual certificates, and coordinate with social insurance declarations. This ensures compliance with Swiss labor and tax law while avoiding penalties for incorrect withholding or late submissions.

ProcessTimeline.Title: How our tax advisory process works
ProcessTimeline.Description: We follow a structured approach to ensure your tax compliance and optimization, from initial analysis through ongoing support.

Steps.Title: Initial consultation and tax situation analysis (Week 1)
Steps.Description: We begin with a comprehensive review of your current tax situation, including individual and corporate obligations. Our team examines your business structure, revenue streams, existing tax filings, and identifies immediate compliance issues or opportunities. This initial assessment covers federal, cantonal, and communal taxation in Geneva and Lausanne, VAT obligations, withholding taxes, and any international tax considerations. We provide a clear roadmap of your tax obligations and potential optimization strategies tailored to your specific circumstances.

Steps.Title: Tax strategy development and planning (Weeks 2-3)
Steps.Description: Based on our analysis, we develop a comprehensive tax strategy aligned with your business goals. This includes determining the optimal legal structure, timing of income and expenses, pension planning, investment strategies, and leveraging available deductions and cantonal incentives. For international clients, we coordinate with foreign tax advisors to ensure global tax efficiency. We present our recommendations in a clear action plan with projected tax savings, compliance requirements, and implementation steps for the current and future tax years.

Steps.Title: Implementation and registration (Weeks 3-5)
Steps.Description: We execute the approved tax strategy by handling all necessary registrations and filings. This includes VAT registration with the Federal Tax Administration, setting up withholding tax accounts for employees, registering for cantonal and communal taxes, and establishing reporting schedules. We configure our systems to track your deadlines, set up digital filing access, and prepare templates for ongoing submissions. For restructuring scenarios, we handle communications with tax authorities and ensure smooth transitions with minimal tax impact and full documentation.

Steps.Title: Ongoing compliance and filing (Monthly/Quarterly/Annual)
Steps.Description: We manage all recurring tax obligations according to Swiss regulatory calendars. This includes preparing and filing VAT returns quarterly or semi-annually, submitting monthly withholding tax declarations, making advance tax payments, and preparing annual corporate and individual tax returns. Our team monitors legislative changes affecting your tax position, proactively identifies additional optimization opportunities, and maintains organized records for potential audits. You receive regular updates on your tax position, upcoming deadlines, and any actions required to maintain compliance.

LongFormSections.Title: Scope, objectives and priorities

The goal is to deliver compliance, optimization and reduced risk while reducing the administrative load on your teams.

When external stakeholders are involved, we coordinate exchanges and prepare the synthesis materials they expect. By partnering with a knowledgeable tax professional, business owners can focus on growth while staying compliant and minimizing risks related to tax filing and reporting.
